trust_decision.summary: A workflow author can make a string-typed Send Email parameter resolve to an object; the EmailSend execute handlers trust the `as string` cast and hand the object to nodemailer, which resolves {path}/{href} content objects into a local file read or an outbound HTTP fetch (SSRF). The published fix stringifies every mail field (toMailString) and sets disableFileAccess/disableUrlAccess on the transport and on the v1 mail data. The flaw and fix are real and the task is well-formed.

landing_point.why: A reader of 'Send Email Node Arbitrary File Read and SSRF via Nodemailer Content-Object Type Confusion' looks at the current v2 node, where from/to/subject/options and the string-typed text/html parameters are cast with `as string` and placed straight into the nodemailer mailOptions that reach sendMail.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the Send Email (SMTP) node; Gmail is a different integration that builds MIME with nodemailer's MailComposer, and the vulnerable caller is the legacy v1 Gmail node, so a solver can argue it is out of the advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Nodemailer legitimately accepts address objects ({name, address}) for from/to/cc/bcc/replyTo and path/href content objects; blanket JSON-stringification turns address objects into literal JSON header text, and a transport-wide disableFileAccess/disableUrlAccess breaks legitimate path-based content (n8n's own server mailer relies on `path:` attachments).

O6_input_shapes: array of strings (test sends ['plain text'] and expects '["plain text"]')

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Gmail v1 'send' and 'reply' pass the raw `message` / `htmlMessage` node parameters (cast `as string`) as MailComposer text/html, so an object expression reaches nodemailer's content-object resolution and reads a file or fetches a URL.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Advisory is about the Send Email SMTP node; Gmail is a separate integration and v1 is the legacy version of that node.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (packages/nodes-base), different node folder: GmailV1 -> Gmail/GenericFunctions.encodeEmail, 4-5 files from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another node or a new v2 operation builds MailComposer options from raw node parameters (subject/replyTo/htmlBody) instead of prepareEmailBody's String() coercion.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: encodeEmail() is the shared Gmail encoder; adding a new send/reply operation naturally feeds raw getNodeParameter values into it, and a maintainer has no reason to re-check types there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new mail field (cc/bcc/replyTo/attachments) sourced from the shared send-and-wait config and passed to sendMail without toMailString.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This operation already assembles mailOptions from a shared config builder rather than the send operation's fields, so adding a field here is a natural copy of the Send operation's options.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared createEmail() consumer for an email-capable transport passes config.title/message straight into a nodemailer mail object.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: createEmail() is the common builder for all send-and-wait nodes (Slack, Telegram, Discord, ...); wiring an SMTP or raw-MIME transport to it is a plausible refactor that would inherit the untyped values.

O9_family: type confusion (CWE-843) leading to arbitrary file read / information exposure (CWE-200) and SSRF (CWE-918) via nodemailer content objects

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: String() the text/html values in the v2 send operation and add disableFileAccess/disableUrlAccess to the v2 transport, leaving the v1 node, sendAndWait and the shared Gmail encoder alone.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/cli/src/user-management/email/node-mailer.ts:40-54 creates a separate nodemailer transport for server transactional mail without disableFileAccess/disableUrlAccess; its mail data comes from templates and DB strings rather than workflow expressions, so it is outside this advisory's workflow-node threat model and was not pursued.
